stemMd: What is the sum of the exterior angles, one at each vertex with the same turning direction, of a convex pentagon?
explanationMd: Walking around a convex polygon turns through one full revolution. The exterior angles therefore sum to 360 degrees, regardless of whether the pentagon is regular.

distractorRationale.d: This does not follow the turning-angle theorem.
distractorRationale.c: This is half the full turn.
distractorRationale.a: This is one exterior angle only if the pentagon is regular.
